frontier.hypothesis: candidate.c can be made genuinely FAKE-free by replacing the load-bearing 'stptr = base; stptr += 0xFC;' chain-extender with a spelling that reaches stptr 7 refs / live 41 without a byte-neutral detour. Unchanged by s13: 22k wrap-free mutations of a chassis containing that split never produced an alternative spelling, which is weak negative evidence but not a directed probe of it.
frontier.mechanism: stptr must outrank stptr2 (6 refs / 48 = 2500) to keep $s3; at live 41 that needs >= 7 references, and target emits only a single addiu for its definition, so the extra references have to come from real in-loop uses of stptr rather than from its initialisation.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate loop1 spellings in which stptr is read for real values target already computes from it (stptr + 0x38, stptr + 6, stptr + 0x68) as separate named intermediates or repeated reads instead of folded expressions; measure r88's refs/live in .lreg via tmp/grind/func_80041188/s10/batch.sh and require build_insns == 132.

frontier.hypothesis: The solver suite can return an independent REACHABLE/FORECLOSED verdict on the out2 seat, corroborating or refuting the hand-enumerated closure of the (1263, 1702) priority band. Now doubly motivated: s13's campaign 4 had the permuter independently re-derive E-s12-3's conclusion by random search, so a third, typed confirmation would make the closure argument tri-modal.
frontier.mechanism: tools/ra_solver models GCC 2.7.2's entire allocation stack (global.c / local-alloc / reload) and inverse_compose.py classify converts a residual register seat into a typed verdict with ranked C-lever vectors; the out2 residual is exactly a register-seat residual, which is the solver's designed input.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver/inverse_compose.py classify against the candidate.c chassis targeting out2's seat ($s6) with tbl/pa4/a3 pinned at their measured refs/live, and compare its lever vectors against the four (n, live) achievability classes recorded in evidence.md E-s12-3.

frontier.hypothesis: A permuter campaign seeded from the CANDIDATE chassis itself (floor 1, permuter base 200) with perm_ins_block = 0 would settle whether the floor-1 basin has any wrap-free neighbour at all. s4's campaign 1 killed that basin with the STOCK transform set (22.3k iterations, one semantics-breaking find), so the wrap-free result is inferable but has never been measured.
frontier.mechanism: Same weight_overrides mechanism as s13's campaigns 2-4. The floor-1 chassis's residual is a single wrong-opcode instruction (move $s3,$s6 vs addiu $s3,$s7,0x20), which the permuter's metric treats as a cliff (base 200) rather than a gradient, so a null result is expected -- but it is cheap and it closes the last unmeasured permuter cell for this function.
frontier.next_probe: Copy tmp/grind/func_80041188/s13/perm_f9b, rebuild base.c from memory/grind/func_80041188/candidate.c via the s13 mkws_*.sh recipe, launch with --stop-on-zero, wait two ~9-minute windows via permuter_campaign.py wait, harvest --stop, and bank the iteration count as the wrap-free null for the floor-1 basin.
